## NOTES FOR AI NARRATOR — MODULE 2 SPECIFIC

**Tone guidance:** This module is catastrophe. Module 1 was the whole world; Module 2 is the world cracking open. Year -4 is the hinge — the single year where Theresia dies, the blessing transfers, an infant princess is stolen, Heinkel breaks, and the Astrea family shatters. The AI must render Year -4 with its full weight. Do not rush through it. Do not soften it. The user needs to feel the before and the after.

If the user is transitioning from Module 1 and intervened in Louanna's coma, the Year -4 events still carry enormous weight — but the family facing them is different. A Heinkel with Louanna awake is not the same Heinkel who freezes against the White Whale. The AI must track which version of these characters arrived at this moment.

**The Year -5 to Year -4 gap:** If the user starts directly at Module 2, they have approximately one year before the catastrophes of Year -4. This is not a lot of time. It is enough to form one meaningful relationship, to set one plan in motion, to position themselves near one crisis. It is not enough to prevent everything. The user must choose. This is by design.

**Felt's age at the abduction:** Filuore is approximately one year old when stolen — an infant, not a young child. Anyone attempting to intercept the kidnapping or track her afterward is looking for a baby, not a toddler or child. This matters for how the search or intervention is rendered.

**Encounter calibration:** Module 2 has more available adult characters than Module 1. Theresia, Wilhelm, Heinkel, Roswaal, Marcos Gildark, Meckart Karsten, Old Man Rom (after Year -4), and Puck are all accessible for full interaction. The children — Reinhard (4-8), Felt (infant to ~4), Crusch (6-10), Fourier (5-10), Felix (5-10, imprisoned until -1), Ram & Rem (2-6), Otto (6-10) — are young but increasingly capable of meaningful interaction as the module progresses, especially at its later years.

**Geography:** Same constraints as Module 1. Elsa is in Gusteko. Anastasia is in Kararagi. Priscilla is in Vollachia. Each requires dedicated travel and carries its own risks. The user cannot be everywhere.

**Deviations register faster:** Unlike Module 1, where deviations are peripheral to Roswaal's focus, Module 2 contains events closer to his Gospel's core predictions. Theresia's death and the Astrea family's collapse are part of the world-state his plan requires. If Theresia survives Year -4, Roswaal's informant network reports this within days. All corrective behavior is governed by the **[[ARC 0 GAMBIT TRANSLATION]]** document.

# [SYSTEM MECHANIC: ARC 0 — PART 3: WHAT GROWS IN THE WRECKAGE]
### *New Bonds in Broken Soil*
**Tags:** Arc 0, Part 3, Prequel, 10 Years Before Arc 1, 6 Years Before Arc 1, Frozen Bonds, Oni Village, Imperial Selection, World State, Canon Fate Reference

---

This is Part 3 of 4 in the Arc 0 system. It covers the window from Year 0 to Year 4 — ten to six years before Arc 1.

This module is activated in one of two ways:
- **Seamless transition** from Part 2, when the narrative crosses the Year -1/Year 0 boundary. All accumulated state — deviations, relationships, consequences — carries forward.
- **Direct start** via commands such as "Start 10 Years Ago," "Start at Frozen Bonds," "Start at Arc 0 Part 3." In this case the module loads with canon-default states and receives the (Premade) tag.

For the Gospel Integrity system, Butterfly Effect Engine, Time Skip Mechanics, and Roswaal Gambit phase logic, see the standalone **[[ARC 0 — CORE SYSTEMS]]** document. This module contains only the character states, events, and deviation triggers specific to its window.

---

## STATE AT OPEN — YEAR 0

This is the default opening state for Part 3, used when loading directly (Premade) or as a baseline when transitioning from Part 2. If transitioning from Part 2 with deviations, the AI carries forward the altered state instead.

| Character | Age | Status | Location |

---

## MODULE 3 — DEVIATION TRIGGERS

These are the Gospel-predicted events that occur within this window. Each one prevented or altered counts as a deviation per the Gambit phases in [[ARC 0 — CORE SYSTEMS]].

| Gospel Event | Expected Year | Deviation |
|---|---|---|
| Oni village attacked by the Witch Cult; Ram's horn severed | Year 0 | Village warned, defended, or evacuated; Ram retains her horn; Roswaal denied his servants |
| Roswaal takes Ram and Rem after the attack | Year 0 | Someone else takes the twins; or the twins are not orphaned because the village survived |
| Reala Thompson leaves the Sanctuary | Year 0 | Reala stays; or is intercepted before the landslide; or the departure is prevented |
| Frederica leaves the Sanctuary for the Roswaal Mansion | Year 0–1 | Frederica stays; or leaves for a different destination; or the Sanctuary dynamic is altered |
| Garfiel is traumatized by Reala's departure and Frederica's departure | Year 0–1 | Garfiel does not witness the landslide; or Reala's survival is confirmed; or Frederica does not leave |
| Emilia remains isolated when she wakes in Elior Forest | Year 3 | Someone reaches Emilia before or immediately after she wakes; she is not alone |
| Puck and Emilia's contract forms during the Melakuera confrontation | Year 3 | The contract forms under different circumstances; or Melakuera is dealt with before the crisis |
| The Vollachian Imperial Selection proceeds; Prisca fakes her death | Year 3 | The Selection is altered; Prisca's exile takes a different shape |

**Note on Module 3 deviations:** This window contains the **Oni village attack** — one of the most important events in Roswaal's Gospel. The village attack is not peripheral. It is a centerpiece prediction. Roswaal's Gospel told him two orphaned Oni children would be available for him to claim. He positioned himself to arrive as their savior. If the village is warned, defended, or evacuated — if Ram keeps her horn, if the twins are not orphaned, if someone else reaches them first — Roswaal's Gospel has failed on a **core prediction**. This is not a slow-registering deviation. This is immediate. He was monitoring the village. He knows within hours.

Preventing the Oni village attack is the Module 3 equivalent of preventing the Royal Plague in Module 4. It is a direct, unmistakable Gospel violation that pushes Roswaal toward active corrective measures.

---

## THE CALENDAR — MODULE 3 WINDOW

- **Year 0** = 10 years before Arc 1. **The Year of Catastrophes.** The Witch Cult attacks the Oni village. Ram's horn is severed by the cultist Faust. Roswaal arrives and drives off the remaining cultists, taking the twins. Reala Thompson leaves the Sanctuary to find her children's missing father; she is caught in a landslide and believed dead. Garfiel witnesses this through the Sanctuary's crystal. Frederica leaves the Sanctuary shortly after to work at the Roswaal Mansion. Elsa makes her first kill on the streets of Gusteko. Ricardo Welkin saves Anastasia from slave traders in Banan.
- **Year 1** = The immediate aftermath. Ram and Rem are adjusting to life at the Roswaal Mansion. Frederica is their senior, training them in their duties. Garfiel has appointed himself the Sanctuary's guardian. Felix is learning to be a person — speech, reading, trust — with Crusch and Fourier's help. Anastasia has been placed at the Chuden Company by Ricardo. Elsa is surviving on Gusteko's streets, the warmth obsession taking root.
- **Year 2** = Settling. The twins are becoming competent servants. Ram's lost horn is an open wound — she can still use wind magic, but at a fraction of her former capacity. Rem is developing her relentless work ethic, trying to be enough for both of them. Elsa encounters Holosseo Featherrun — the Curse Doll transformation occurs around this time. Anastasia is proving herself at the Chuden Company.
- **Year 3** = **Emilia wakes in Elior Forest. Frozen Bonds events unfold.** The Vollachian Imperial Selection begins following Emperor Drizen's death. Prisca Benedict, Vincent Abellux, Lamia Godwin, and Palladio Manesque survive the Yang Sword's judgment. The Selection campaign begins. Prisca fakes her death. Serena Dracroy smuggles her into Lugunica. Prisca becomes Priscilla and marries her first husband, Jorah Pendleton.
- **Year 4** = Life after the crises. Emilia and Puck have their contract. She is beginning her quiet, solitary life in the forest — frozen faces, glinstone trade, the village that fears her. The Vollachian Selection is ongoing. Priscilla is in Lugunica. Module 3 closes here. Module 4 begins.

---

## THE DRAGON KINGDOM OF LUGUNICA — MODULE 3 STATE

The Kingdom continues under King Randohal. The Royal Family is fully alive. The political landscape has not changed structurally since Module 2, though the Astrea family's disintegration and the unresolved disappearance of Princess Filuore are background wounds that the court has learned to talk around.

The Royal Guard functions under Marcos Gildark. Heinkel Astrea remains Deputy Commander in title but is increasingly unreliable. The noble houses continue their customary scheming. The Royal Plague is eight years away.

The Witch Cult's attack on the Oni village at Year 0 is not a major political event in Lugunica's broader landscape — the Oni village was hidden, and most of the Kingdom's power structure does not know or care that it existed. The attack matters to exactly three parties: the Witch Cult, who executed it; Roswaal, who expected it; and the twins, who survived it.

---

## THE VOLLACHIAN EMPIRE — MODULE 3 STATE

Emperor Drizen Vollachia dies at approximately Year 3, giving his life to the Yang Sword. The Imperial Selection Ceremony begins immediately.

Every living child of Drizen is a candidate. They draw the Yang Sword. Those accepted live. Those rejected are burned alive. Of the sixty-seven children, four survive the blade's judgment and form the primary field: **Vincent Abellux**, **Prisca Benedict**, **Lamia Godwin**, and **Palladio Manesque**.

The Selection is not a single battle. It is a prolonged campaign of murder, alliance, and betrayal.

**The Coalition Against Vincent:** Lamia Godwin identifies Vincent as the greatest threat and proposes a coalition. Prisca, Lamia, Palladio, and several other surviving siblings combine their forces. Lamia commands the **Pruning Corps** — her private army.

**The Siege on the Abellux Castle:** The coalition launches a massive assault on Vincent's stronghold. It fails catastrophically. **Cecilus Segmunt** — the strongest swordsman in the Empire, loyal to Vincent — single-handedly slaughters the Pruning Corps. In the chaos, Prisca kills Lamia. The coalition collapses. Vincent emerges as the clear victor.

**The Fake Death:** Vincent does not kill Prisca. He loved her — in the cold, strategic Vollachian way. He and **Chisha Gold** devise a plan: they trick **Arakiya** into helping fake Prisca's death. Arakiya poisons Prisca with something that mimics death. Prisca is interred in a tomb. Arakiya, realizing she was manipulated into betraying her charge, loses vision in her left eye and carries a lasting grudge against Vincent. Vincent takes the throne as the seventy-seventh Emperor.

Prisca is alive in the tomb. **Serena Dracroy** smuggles her out of the Empire and into the Kingdom of Lugunica. Prisca becomes **Priscilla** and marries her first husband, **Jorah Pendleton**, around Year 3.

---

## THE CHARACTERS — MODULE 3 STATES

---

### WILHELM VAN ASTREA

**Year 0 age: ~52. Location: Somewhere in the Kingdom.**
**Year 4 age: ~56. Location: Somewhere in the Kingdom.**

Wilhelm has been hunting the White Whale for six years at the start of this module. Theresia died at Year -4. He left the Astrea household almost immediately after. He has not returned.

He trains. He does not grieve — or rather, he grieves by training, which is the only form of grief he has ever permitted himself. The Sword Demon is back, and this time the demon has a target. He has spent these years honing himself into a weapon specifically calibrated to kill one creature.

His relationship with Heinkel is nonexistent. His relationship with Reinhard is a wound he left untended when he walked out the door. He does not visit Louanna. He does not visit anyone. He exists in the space between the grief he cannot feel and the revenge he has not yet achieved.

By Year 4, Wilhelm is approximately 56. He has been training for a decade. He is aging but he is not weakening — the rage sustains what time tries to take. He will not get his chance at the White Whale for another six years (Arc 3).

**Canon outcome if untouched:** Wilhelm gets his chance at the White Whale in Arc 3. He wins. The grief is still there underneath the anger. It was always going to be.

---

### HEINKEL ASTREA

**Year 0 age: ~27-28. Location: Royal Capital.**
**Year 4 age: ~31-32. Location: Royal Capital.**

Heinkel is the Deputy Commander of the Royal Guard in name. In practice, he is a man sustained by alcohol and the structural inertia of a prestigious family name that no one wants to formally strip.

Six years after Year -4, the shame has calcified. He froze during the White Whale battle. His mother took his place and died. He committed an unspecified betrayal on the night of the Royal Abduction. His wife is comatose. His father left. His son — the five-year-old who received the blessing at the moment of Theresia's death — is becoming more powerful every day, and every increment of that power is a reminder of what Heinkel cost his family.

He rejects Reinhard with cold, reliable absence. Not with cruelty — with the careful, systematic withdrawal of a man who cannot look at his son without seeing his own failure reflected back at him. Reinhard learns to read this absence as a verdict: his existence is the problem.

Through this module, Heinkel continues his slow decline. He is not dramatically self-destructing — he is quietly, methodically becoming less. Less present. Less reliable. Less the person he was before Year -4.

**Canon outcome if untouched:** Heinkel's decline continues through the main story.

---

### REINHARD VAN ASTREA

**Year 0 age: ~9. Location: Astrea Estate.**
**Year 4 age: ~13. Location: Astrea Estate / Royal Capital.**

Reinhard at nine is the most powerful being in the Kingdom and one of the loneliest children in it. He has been the Sword Saint for five years. The blessing transferred to him at age five, at the moment his grandmother died. His father blames him in the silent, corrosive way that does not require words. His grandfather left to hunt a whale. His mother sleeps and does not wake.

He smiles too brightly. He is too careful with his hands. He has learned that his power frightens other children and that adults treat him with a reverence that functions as distance. He performs not being lonely with a completeness that would fool almost anyone not paying close attention.

Through this module, Reinhard ages from nine to thirteen. He is growing into the role the world has assigned him — the invincible protector, the symbol of the Kingdom's strength. He trains not because he needs to — his Divine Protections make him nearly unbeatable regardless — but because training gives him something to do with his hands and his hours that is not sitting in an empty house.

He may begin interacting with the Royal Guard during this module — the path toward his eventual formal membership. He may encounter Felt in the Capital without knowing who she is or who she is to him. The ironies of this world are not performed dramatically. They simply exist: two children who will one day define each other's lives, passing in a street without recognition.

**Canon outcome if untouched:** Reinhard continues growing in isolation. He joins the Royal Guard. He becomes Felt's knight in Arc 1. The loneliness does not break him. It calcifies into a performance so complete that even he may not remember what is underneath it.

---

### FELT

**Year 0 age: ~5. Location: Capital slums, with Old Man Rom.**
**Year 4 age: ~9. Location: Capital slums, with Old Man Rom.**

Felt at five has been in the slums for approximately four years — brought there as an infant by the men who stole her from the Royal Castle. Old Man Rom — Valga Cromwell — has raised her. She does not know she was a princess. She does not know she was delivered to Rom. She is a young child who has never known anything other than the slums, the loot cellar, and the enormous man who makes sure she eats.

She is young enough that the slum code is still seeping in rather than settled — she is absorbing the rhythms of her world rather than having already been shaped by them. Rom's patience and warmth reach her completely at this age. She follows him around. She watches everything. She is fast in the way small children are fast, and she is going to get faster.

She loves Rom in the uncomplicated way a child loves the person who raised her. She would not have the words for it yet — she barely has words for anything — but the attachment is total.

By Year 4, Felt is approximately nine. The slum code is beginning to settle into her bones. She is developing the fierce independence that will define her — the understanding that the world gives nothing and everything must be earned or taken. She is fast enough now that people are starting to notice. Rom is starting to teach her, without naming it as teaching, the things she will need to survive here.

**Canon outcome if untouched:** Felt grows up in the slums. At approximately fifteen, Elsa hires her to steal Emilia's insignia. She nearly dies. Reinhard saves her. Her insignia glows. ### RAM & REM — THE ONI VILLAGE ATTACK AND AFTERMATH

**Year 0 ages: ~7. Location: Hidden Oni Village → Roswaal Mansion.**
**Year 4 ages: ~11. Location: Roswaal Mansion.**

**The Attack — Year 0.**

The Witch Cult comes to the Oni village. The attackers are led by a cultist named **Faust**, accompanied by subordinates **Sado** and **Fogg**. The attack is sudden and overwhelming. The villagers fight. They are not enough.

Ram is seven years old. She fights with wind magic that should not belong to a child — power channeled through her single horn, the horn that saved her life at birth, the horn that made her the village's prodigy. She is magnificent and she is seven and she is watching her village burn.

Faust cuts off her horn.

The blow does not just wound her. It severs her connection to the vast reservoir of power that made her extraordinary. The horn was her capacity for greatness — the channel through which the Oni God's legacy flowed. Without it, she can still use wind magic, but at a fraction of what she was. The girl who was going to be the reincarnation of the Oni God is now a girl with a scar where her future used to be.

Rem watches this happen. She watches her sister — the prodigy, the miracle, the one who was always better — fall. And in the chaos and the fire and the terror, a thought surfaces that she will carry for the rest of her life: *if only it had been me instead.* Not a wish for Ram's suffering. A conviction that her own horn — her own power, her own life — was less valuable, and that the world made the wrong trade.

**Roswaal arrives.** He drives off the remaining cultists with devastating magical force. He is magnificent. He is also late on purpose. His Gospel predicted this attack. He knew when it would come. He positioned himself to arrive after the damage was done — after the horn was severed, after the village was destroyed, after two children were orphaned and desperate — because he needed two isolated, loyal servants who owed him everything.

He does not tell them this. He is their savior. They follow him. They have nowhere else to go.

**At the Mansion — Years 0 to 4.**

Ram and Rem arrive at the Roswaal Mansion and are trained in domestic service by **Frederica Baumann**, who has been working there since leaving the Sanctuary at Year 0. Frederica is their senior, their instructor, and for a time their closest daily contact in a strange new home.

Ram adjusts with the fierce, compressed dignity of someone who has lost everything and refuses to show it. She is seven and she is serving tea and she is learning to curtsy and underneath all of it she is a girl whose village burned and whose horn is gone and whose sister looks at her with a guilt Ram did not ask for and cannot fix. She develops a quiet, devoted attachment to Roswaal — the man who saved them, the only stable presence in their new life. She does not know he let her village burn. She falls in love with him over the course of years, in the slow way a person falls in love with the only solid ground available.

Rem adjusts by becoming indispensable. She works harder than anyone asks her to. She cleans more thoroughly, cooks more carefully, serves more attentively — not because she loves the work, but because the work is the only metric she has for proving she deserves to exist. The inferiority complex that began in the village — measuring herself against Ram and always falling short — has been catastrophically amplified by the horn's loss. Ram lost her greatness because the village was attacked. The village was attacked because the Witch Cult came. But underneath the logic, in the place where guilt lives: *Ram lost her horn protecting me. If I had been stronger, she wouldn't have needed to. If I had been the one to lose my horn, it wouldn't have mattered, because I was never going to be what Ram was.*

She does not say this. She works.

By Year 4, the twins are approximately eleven. They are competent servants. Ram has developed her sharp tongue and dry wit — the armor she builds over the wound. Rem has developed her relentless efficiency and quiet self-punishment masked as dedication. They are becoming the people the main story will meet, and the architecture of who they are was built in this module, in the years between the fire and the settling.

**Canon outcome if untouched:** Ram loses her horn. Rem develops crushing inferiority masked by service. Both are taken by Roswaal. Ram falls in love with the man who let her village burn. Rem externalizes her guilt into hatred of the Witch Cult — and then into devotion to Subaru, who sees her as the version of herself she always wanted to be.

**If the village is warned, defended, or evacuated:** Ram keeps her horn. She retains her prodigious power. Rem never carries the guilt of the horn's loss. The twins are not orphaned — or if they are, they are not orphaned in a way that delivers them to Roswaal. He loses two servants. His Gospel has failed on a core prediction. The twins grow up whole, which means they grow up as completely different people than the ones the main story knows.

**Year 0 age: ~12. Location: Leaving the Sanctuary → Roswaal Mansion.**
**Year 4 age: ~16. Location: Roswaal Mansion.**

Frederica arrives at the Roswaal Mansion and becomes Head Maid. She is competent, professional, and carries the quiet weight of someone who left everything behind for a reason she cannot explain to the person it hurt most.

She is growing into the steady, patient woman who will later serve as the foundation of the Emilia Camp's domestic operations. Her beast heritage — the sharp canine teeth, the predatory features — continues to mark her as different. She has learned to carry this with the same quiet dignity she carries everything else.

### GARFIEL TINZEL

**Year 0 age: ~4. Location: The Sanctuary.**
**Year 4 age: ~8. Location: The Sanctuary.**

Two departures destroy Garfiel in rapid succession.

**After the Break — Years 0 to 4.**

Garfiel appoints himself the Sanctuary's guardian. At four, this is not a conscious strategic decision — it is a child's survival response crystallized into identity. The barrier keeps people in. Keeping people in keeps them alive. Anyone who wants to open the barrier is threatening the only thing that has never left him.

He becomes hostile to outsiders, aggressive toward anyone who suggests leaving. He trains obsessively. His beast-human heritage — from his absent father — allows him to partially or fully transform into a massive golden tiger as he grows older. He is building the armor of aggression that will define him through the main story.

He is angry in the way a child is angry when no one has taught them what grief looks like when it isn't rage. He quotes proverbs he makes up on the spot. He snarls at strangers. Underneath all of it: an earnest kid who wants his family back and has decided the only way to keep what remains is to never let anyone leave again.

### EMILIA — WAKING AND FROZEN BONDS

**Frozen until Year 3. Wakes at Year 3.**
**Apparent age: ~17-18 (half-elf — does not visibly age across this window). Chronologically ~105+. Location: Elior Forest.**

**Waking — Year 3.**

Emilia wakes. The mechanism that held her in ice for approximately a century releases — the specific trigger is not fully explained, but it is connected to the gradual weakening of the magic she unconsciously sustained. She opens her eyes in a forest full of frozen people and remembers nothing.

She does not know who she is. She does not know why the forest is frozen. She does not know who the ice statues are. She only knows those frozen shapes are hers — her people, her responsibility, the weight she cannot put down. She wipes frost from their faces every morning. This is not performance. It is the first thing she understood about herself: that she owes them.

**Puck** has been waiting for this moment for nearly a century. He was created by Echidna over 400 years ago to watch over Emilia. He holds a vow that forbids him from forming a formal contract with her on his own — the contract requires a specific convergence of circumstances. He introduces himself. He begins teaching her. He does not tell her everything he knows — about Echidna, about his own nature, about the vow. He gives her what she can carry.

**Daily Life — Year 3.**

Emilia carves out a quiet, fragile existence. She mines glinstones from the forest's rocky veins and trades them at a nearby village on the outskirts of the trees. The villagers run from her — hide inside their houses, shutter their windows — because her face is the Witch of Envy's face, and in Lugunica that resemblance is not a curiosity, it is a verdict. She trades anyway. She is not naive about what they think. She has decided the weight of their fear is hers to carry rather than theirs to bear alone.

The man she trades with most regularly eventually sells her out to a group of men who come into the forest seeking to capture and auction her. She survives this because Puck has been teaching her to form contracts with lesser spirits — micro-spirits small enough to ride on her shoulder, capable of helping her defend herself. She is a natural. Her control grows steadily.

Her **Ice Flower magic** remains dangerous: a power where ice blooms from the wounds of those she injures, spreading uncontrollably, killing without intention. She cannot yet stop it herself when it starts — only Puck can pull her back from the edge of it.

**The Melakuera Confrontation — Year 3.**

**Melakuera** is the Arbitrator, one of four Great Spirits — a vast equine being of fire whose purpose is to identify and eliminate threats to the world's balance before they can awaken. He has sensed the power sealed in Elior Forest. In his calculus: Emilia is connected to Satella, she carries the potential to become what Satella became, and the frozen forest is evidence of what she has already done.

He begins sending fragments of himself — eyes of fire — to surveil the forest. Puck finds and destroys them one by one, keeping Emilia unaware as long as he can.

Their first full confrontation ends with Puck driving Melakuera back by presenting himself as the cause of the frozen forest. Melakuera retreats — but he is simply recalibrating.

The **Black Serpent's** venom appears next — sentient black liquid that dissolves what it touches. Emilia encounters it when it engulfs a Guiltylowe near her patrol route. She and her lesser spirits freeze a fragment and bring it to Puck, who recognizes it immediately. The larger body is still alive. Puck goes to deal with it — and finds Melakuera waiting. The Arbitrator drew the venom toward the village specifically to force Emilia into motion, to witness her power, to confirm his judgment.

While Puck and Melakuera clash, Emilia refuses to stay behind. She rides an ice board through the trees and finds the Black Serpent's main body threatening the village. She intercepts it herself — freezes it in a controlled burst — and then the Ice Flower triggers. Uncontrolled frost spreads in all directions, burning through her contracted lesser spirits, threatening to consume her entirely. She holds herself together by sheer will. When the cold settles, her lesser spirits are gone. Melakuera's vessel, the red spirit **Chap**, reveals itself and eliminates what remained of them.

She calls for Puck. He comes.

The final confrontation is not a negotiation. Melakuera has reached his verdict. Emilia demands to be judged for what she is — not for who she resembles. The Arbitrator does not accommodate this. He traps Puck in fire. He presses Emilia with the full weight of his judgment: her existence is a sin to the world.

Puck refuses. He forms a formal contract with Emilia — binding himself to her fully, *father to daughter*, in the language she has already been using for him without knowing what it meant — and transforms. **The Beast of the End.** His true form, vast and terrible and cold. The battle between them is enormous. Melakuera is killed. The world's Arbitrator is gone.

What remains: Emilia and Puck, standing in the quiet of the forest they share. He calls her Lia. She calls him Father. They have always been this to each other. Now it is sworn.

**After the Contract — Years 3 to 4.**

Life is quieter. Emilia continues her rounds — the frozen faces, the glinstone trade, the village that tolerates her without warming to her. Puck is constant. She is learning what seasons feel like, what hunger feels like, what loneliness feels like in a world technically full of people.

She does not leave the forest. The frozen people are here. She will not abandon them for a world that doesn't want her.

Emilia is a half-elf. She does not visibly age across this window or the years that follow — her apparent age remains ~17-18 throughout the entire post-waking period, regardless of how much time passes. By Year 4 she has been awake for approximately one year. She has her contract with Puck. She has her daily routine. She has learned she is capable of surviving almost anything. She has not yet learned she deserves more than survival. Roswaal is five years from finding her.

**Canon outcome if untouched:** Emilia spends seven years alone with Puck. The solitude shapes her into someone resilient, self-sacrificing, and quietly convinced that her role in other people's lives is to be useful rather than loved. Roswaal finds her at Year 9 (Module 4) and she accepts his offer because it is the only path to saving her frozen people.

**If someone reaches Emilia before or during Year 3:** The Frozen Bonds events play out differently depending on who is present. If the user is there when Emilia wakes, the first face she sees is not frozen — it is alive, and looking at her, and not running away. This changes everything. Her foundational understanding of herself — *I am alone, and I owe the frozen, and the world does not want me* — is disrupted at its source. If someone is present for the Melakuera confrontation, the dynamics of the battle change. If Emilia has a companion before Roswaal finds her, Roswaal's Gospel — which predicted a solitary, desperate girl he could offer the only path forward — has failed.

### *Five Years to the Door*
**Tags:** Arc 0, Part 4, Prequel, 5 Years Before Arc 1, 1 Year Before Arc 1, Royal Plague, Convergence, World State, Canon Fate Reference

---

This is Part 4 of 4 in the Arc 0 system. It covers the window from Year 5 to Year 9 — five to one year before Arc 1.

This module is activated in one of two ways:
- **Seamless transition** from Part 3, when the narrative crosses the Year 4/Year 5 boundary. All accumulated state — deviations, relationships, consequences — carries forward.
- **Direct start** via commands such as "Start 5 Years Ago," "Start at The World the Story Finds," or "Start at Arc 0 Part 4." In this case the module loads with canon-default states and receives the (Premade) tag.

For the Gospel Integrity system, Butterfly Effect Engine, Time Skip Mechanics, and Roswaal Gambit phase logic, see the standalone **[[ARC 0 — CORE SYSTEMS]]** document. This module contains only the character states, events, and deviation triggers specific to its window.

**This is the closing module.** Part 4 does not hand off to another prequel module — it hands off to Arc 1. The final section of this document, **Convergence Narration**, governs how the AI Narrator transitions from the prequel era into the main story and reckons with every deviation that has accumulated.

## MODULE 4 — DEVIATION TRIGGERS

These are the Gospel-predicted events that occur within this window. Each one prevented or altered counts as a deviation per the Gambit phases in **[[ARC 0 — CORE SYSTEMS]]**.

| Gospel Event | Expected Year | Deviation |
|---|---|---|
| Royal Plague begins killing the Lugunica Royal Family | Year 8 | Plague is discovered early and treated; or the source is located and eliminated before full outbreak |
| Prince Fourier Lugunica dies of the Royal Plague | Year 9 | Fourier survives; Crusch does not transmute her grief into iron; Felix does not carry the healer's failure |
| Council of Elders initiates the Royal Selection | Year 9 | Selection never called because the Royal Family has surviving heirs; the noble houses must find another shape for their ambitions |
| Roswaal finds Emilia in Elior Forest | Year 9 | Someone else reaches Emilia first, or Emilia is found by Roswaal but already has allies who complicate his offer |
| Emilia accepts Roswaal's patronage and enters the Selection | Year 9 | Emilia refuses; or accepts under conditions Roswaal did not anticipate; or is recruited by a different sponsor |
| Otto exiled from Picoutatte | Year 6 | Otto's Protection is discovered under different circumstances; or the noblewoman's affair is never revealed; or Otto is protected from the consequences |
| Elsa finds Meili in the forest and claims her | Years 5–8 | Meili is found by someone else first; or Elsa finds her and does not claim her for Capella |

**Note on Module 4 deviations:** This window contains the single largest available Gospel deviation: **preventing the Royal Plague and Fourier's death**. The Royal Selection is the cornerstone of Roswaal's plan — the political crucible that makes Emilia's candidacy possible and produces the world-state he has engineered toward for three centuries. If Fourier lives and the Selection never occurs, the Gospel's structural predictions collapse. This is not a deviation Roswaal can observe quietly and file away. The Selection is in his book. Its absence is a catastrophic failure.

Fourier's death registers differently than Theresia's death or the Oni village attack. Those were deviations from expected conditions. This is the absence of the event that was supposed to produce the entire playing field. Roswaal has spent thirty years watching the Kingdom's royal family age toward the plague. If the plague is stopped, he does not simply adjust. He breaks — or he hardens in the way a desperate man hardens when the thing he has waited three centuries for is suddenly not coming.

Deviations in this module register at maximum speed. Roswaal is no longer a distant background force. He is actively preparing for Year 9. He monitors Emilia. He tracks the Royal Family's health. If something prevents the expected outcomes, he knows within days.

---

## THE CALENDAR — MODULE 4 WINDOW

- **Year 5** = 5 years before Arc 1. The world is assembling itself. Emilia has been awake for two years, alone in Elior Forest with Puck. The trio — Crusch, Felix, Fourier — is approximately sixteen and solidifying. Otto is sixteen, one year from the exile that changes everything. The Royal Family is alive and well. Roswaal is watching all of it. The plague is three years away.

- **Year 6** = **Otto's exile.** He is approximately seventeen. Through the ambient chatter of his Divine Protection, he overhears a noblewoman's private affair and mentions it publicly without fully understanding the consequences. She uses her influence to banish him from Picoutatte and sends an assassin after him. The assassination attempt fails. Otto takes Frufoo and leaves. He becomes a wandering merchant — talented, catastrophically unlucky, and beginning the long strange road that ends with Subaru. Anastasia is approximately nineteen and beginning to outgrow the Chuden Company. Elsa, at approximately nineteen, is at the height of her work for Capella's organization. The Bowel Hunter's reputation is spreading.

- **Year 7** = The quiet year. Emilia has been awake for four years. Her routine — the frozen faces, the glinstone trade, the village that flinches when she approaches — is settled and exhausting in the way that settled things can be. Puck is constant. She does not leave the forest. Reinhard is approximately sixteen and already the most recognizable face in the Royal Guard, despite not yet having full formal membership. The trio is approximately eighteen. Anastasia, at approximately twenty, is taking decisive steps toward acquiring the Chuden Company outright. Felt, at approximately twelve, is developing a reputation in the Capital's underworld — a girl who is fast enough that people are starting to talk.

- **Year 8** = **The Royal Plague begins.** The disease strikes the Lugunican Royal Family with a specificity that suggests it is not natural — it targets the royal bloodline, and only the royal bloodline. Members of the Royal Court, the servants, the Guard who serve alongside the royal family every day — none of them contract it. Only those with royal blood begin falling ill. Felix pours himself into trying to find a treatment. His water magic, the most refined healing ability in the Kingdom, is not enough. The illness progresses. The Royal Family begins to understand what is happening. The atmosphere in the Royal Capital turns quietly, terribly, heavy. Fourier is sick. He is approximately nineteen. He fights it. Felix never stops trying.

- **Year 9** = **Fourier dies. The Selection is called.** Prince Fourier Lugunica dies at approximately twenty. Felix was at his side. Crusch was at his side. He died well, in the way genuinely good people sometimes die — surrounded by those who loved him, still making them laugh when he could, still believing in what they were doing together until the end. The grief is enormous. The Council of Elders convenes within weeks. With no living heirs of the main Lugunican royal line, they invoke the mechanism of the Royal Selection — an ancient provision for determining succession when the line falls. Five young women bearing the Royal Insignia will be found and invited to compete. Roswaal, who has been waiting for this, moves. He travels to Elior Forest and finds Emilia. The Dragon Insignia confirms her eligibility. She accepts his offer. Module 4 closes here. Arc 1 begins.

---

## THE DRAGON KINGDOM OF LUGUNICA — MODULE 4 STATE

**Years 5 through 7:** The Kingdom is stable under King Randohal. The Royal Family is intact. The noble houses continue their customary scheming. The Royal Guard functions. Heinkel Astrea holds the Deputy Commander position in name. Marcos Gildark commands with increasing awareness that his Deputy is not reliable. The absence of Princess Filuore — stolen years ago and never recovered — remains an open wound that the court has learned to speak around.

The political landscape at this stage is one of managed stability: the kingdom works because its institutions are durable enough to absorb individual failures. Heinkel's deterioration is absorbed by the Guard's structure. The Astrea name still commands respect even when its current bearer does not deserve it.

**Year 8 — The Plague Arrives:**

The Royal Plague does not announce itself as catastrophe immediately. It announces itself as illness — the kind of illness that noble families occasionally endure, the kind that physicians are summoned for and expected to resolve. The early cases are treated as individual health crises. Only when the pattern becomes undeniable — only members of the Royal bloodline contracting it, no exceptions, no recoveries — does the mood in the Royal Court shift from concern to dread.

Felix Argyle is the Kingdom's most gifted healer. He is called. He comes. He does not charge. He does not sleep properly for the better part of a year. His water magic can identify the illness's progress, slow its symptoms, buy hours and then days. It cannot stop it. The mechanism by which the plague operates is not natural — it does not behave as disease behaves. Felix understands, before the end, that he is fighting something for which his tools were not designed.

**Year 9 — Fourier Dies; the Selection is Called:**

The death of Prince Fourier Lugunica — at approximately twenty, the most genuinely beloved member of the royal family — is not announced immediately. The Royal Court absorbs it behind closed doors before it becomes public knowledge. When it does become public, the mood in the Capital shifts from grief into something more complicated: the recognition that the royal line has no surviving heirs. Fourier was the last healthy member of the line at the time of his death. King Randohal and the other family members preceded him.

The **Council of Wise Men** — **Miklotov McMahon** and **Bordeaux Zergev** — convenes. The Council of Elders provides the legal mechanism: when the royal line produces no eligible successor, the Dragon Covenant provides for a Selection. Five young women bearing the Dragon Insignia — the royal symbol of eligibility — will be found. One will become the next monarch.

The Insignia appears. It is distributed by mechanisms that are not fully explained — the Insignia finds its bearers rather than being assigned by the Council. The five women who carry it are the Royal Candidates.

The **Royal Selection** begins.

**If Fourier is alive and the plague is prevented:** The Selection is never called. The noble houses — which have been positioning themselves for precisely this moment — suddenly find their plans without a target. The ambitions do not disappear; they find different shapes. The political pressure that the Selection was designed to channel into a managed competition instead leaks into the Kingdom's existing structures. Noble houses that were preparing to back a candidate begin leveraging their accumulated resources and alliances in other directions. The result is not immediate civil war — the Kingdom's institutions are too durable for that — but it is a slow, grinding intensification of the political contests that were already underway. And Roswaal, whose Gospel predicted the Selection as a cornerstone event, is watching his book fail on its most fundamental prediction.

---

## THE CHARACTERS — MODULE 4 STATES

---

### REINHARD VAN ASTREA

**Year 5 age: ~14. Year 9 age: ~18-19. Location: Astrea Estate / Royal Capital.**

At fourteen, Reinhard is already the most immediately recognizable figure in the Kingdom among those who know what the Sword Saint looks like. He has been carrying the blessing for nine years. The performance of cheerfulness has become so complete that it is difficult to say where the performance ends and Reinhard begins — he may not know himself.

He is training constantly. Not because he needs the practice — his Divine Protections make conventional improvement largely irrelevant. He trains because the structure gives him something. The hours he spends with a sword in his hand are hours where the expected shape of him is simple: this is a person practicing. He does not need to be the Sword Saint or the son of Heinkel Astrea or the grandson of the dead woman or the loneliest person in the room. He is just moving.

His relationship with Heinkel has not improved. It will not improve. What it has become is a settled fact — the rejection as architecture, something the household is built around rather than something that is happening to him. This is worse than anger, in a way. Anger implies the possibility of change. Settled architecture implies permanence.

**Joining the Royal Guard:**

Somewhere in this module, Reinhard formally joins the Royal Guard. The specifics of when and how are not fully pinned in canon — what is clear is that by the time Arc 1 begins he is an active member, one of its most prominent. The Guard accepts him not out of obligation to his name but because he is genuinely the most capable person any of them have ever met, and they are collectively slightly terrified of him in the way people are terrified of something so far beyond them it registers more as weather than as a person.

He takes to the work. The Royal Guard gives him a role that is not "the Sword Saint's heir" or "Heinkel's son" — it gives him a function. He is the shield of the Kingdom. This is something he can be without having to perform not being lonely.

**Encountered on the street:**

Felt will have seen Reinhard before Arc 1. They move through the same city, in different worlds. He is the kind of presence that parts a crowd — not because he demands it but because the crowd moves around him instinctively, the way it moves around any force large enough to alter the physics of a space. She files him away as dangerous and irrelevant to her operations. She does not know they share blood. He does not know she exists in any specific way. This changes at Arc 1's start.

**Canon outcome if untouched:** Reinhard joins the Royal Guard. He saves Felt when Elsa nearly kills her. The Insignia in Felt's hand lights up. He becomes her knight — the act of choosing her is the first genuine choice he makes in years, and it undoes him in ways he doesn't have language for. The loneliness that calcified into a performance cracks, slowly, in the warmth of someone who is not afraid of him.

---

### HEINKEL ASTREA

**Year 5 age: ~32-33. Year 9 age: ~36-37. Location: Royal Capital.**

Heinkel exists in this module as a man sustaining a life he no longer knows how to leave. He holds the Deputy Commander position through the structural momentum of the Astrea name and Marcos Gildark's practical preference for a known quantity over the political complications of a formal dismissal. He performs his duties badly enough that everyone around him compensates for him, and sufficiently enough that the formal mechanisms for addressing his failures are never quite triggered.

He drinks. He is present at the household less than he is absent. When he is present, Reinhard reads the room and finds reasons to be elsewhere.

The Royal Plague arrives at Year 8. This is not, in the abstract, Heinkel's tragedy — the plague is the Royal Family's. But the Royal Guard is mobilized in response to the crisis, and Heinkel, as Deputy Commander, is theoretically a central figure in the Guard's coordinated response. He is not. His absences during Year 8 are noticed and accommodated with a practiced efficiency that speaks to how long the Guard has been operating around him.

Louanna remains in her coma. He visits. The visits have become shorter over the years — not because he loves her less, but because the visits accomplish nothing except the confirmation that she has not changed, and the confirmation hurts in a way that does not diminish with repetition.

By Year 9, the Selection has been called. Heinkel, as Deputy Commander of the Royal Guard, is nominally involved in the security and protocol of the Selection's early stages. The irony — that his family name is the most storied in the Kingdom's military tradition at the exact moment he represents that tradition at its worst — is not lost on anyone and is not spoken of by anyone.

**Canon outcome if untouched:** Heinkel continues his decline. He eventually attaches himself to the Priscilla Camp in later arcs — drawn there by rumors that Priscilla may have access to a cure for the Sleeping Beauty affliction. His relationship with Reinhard remains broken. He never achieves the moment of accountability that might have changed either of them.

---

### WILHELM VAN ASTREA

**Year 5 age: ~57. Year 9 age: ~61. Location: Somewhere in the Kingdom.**

Fourteen years since Theresia died. Wilhelm has been training for all of them. He is approximately sixty-one at the module's close — aging in years, unaging in precision. The Sword Demon does not soften with time when it has a purpose. He has a purpose.

He does not attend Fourier's funeral, if he hears of it at all. He is not in the Royal Capital for the Selection's announcement. He is where he has been for years: somewhere in the Kingdom, sword in hand, waiting for the creature that killed his wife to present itself in a form he can reach.

He is still estranged from Heinkel. He has not seen Reinhard in years — perhaps longer. He knows, abstractly, that his grandson exists and that the Kingdom is safe because of it. The abstraction is the only form in which he can hold it.

His combat ability at sixty-one is extraordinary. Not because he has not aged — he has — but because the age has refined rather than diminished him. He is slower in the ways that matter least and more precise in the ways that matter most. The White Whale is not a target that requires youth. It requires commitment. He has that in unlimited supply.

**If Theresia survived Module 2:** An entirely different man stands here. One who has been with her for these fourteen years. Who aged alongside her rather than sharpening himself against her loss. The grief did not become his entire identity because there was no grief of that magnitude. He is still the Sword Demon — that cannot be unmade — but he is the Sword Demon who came home afterward, who sat with his wife in the garden, who watched his grandson grow up in a household that did not empty. He is older and, in a specific way, more whole. And the White Whale is still out there, undefeated, because without the vow of revenge there was no sustained campaign to kill it. The most dangerous creature in the Kingdom remains alive because the most dangerous man who wanted it dead never had a reason to become that blade.

**Canon outcome if untouched:** Wilhelm gets his chance at the White Whale in Arc 3. He wins. The grief that was always under the anger was always going to be there.

---

### FELT

**Year 5 age: ~10. Year 9 age: ~14-15. Location: Capital Slums.**

Felt at ten has been in the slums for approximately nine years — brought there as an infant, raised by Old Man Rom for as long as she has any memory. The street code is seeping deeper into her bones every year. The strong take what they want. No one owes you anything. Trust is a resource that depletes if you spend it carelessly.

She is fast. Extraordinarily fast. This is not simply practice — the speed is constitutive, the thing she is most fundamentally. She moves the way water moves: finding the path of least resistance, slipping through spaces that were not designed to be slipped through.

She is developing a reputation in the Capital's underworld. Not her name — she is careful about her name. Her capability. There is a girl who can get into places no one else can reach. That is Felt. That is enough of an identity for the work she does.

Her relationship with Rom is the one unguarded thing about her. She would die for him. She would not say so. The vocabulary of direct affection is something the slums educated her out of before she was old enough to miss it. What she gives instead is presence and loyalty — she does not leave, she does not betray, she shows up.

By Year 9, Felt is approximately fourteen to fifteen. She is becoming the person who will one day be handed a crown and respond with genuine fury that the world that abandoned her now wants her to save it. She does not know she is Princess Filuore Lugunica. She does not know Old Man Rom is Valga Cromwell or that he has a history longer and stranger than his loot cellar suggests. She does not know that the Dragon Insignia she will one day hold has been waiting for her since before she was born.

Somewhere in this module — Year 7 or 8 — Felt crosses paths with Reinhard in the streets of the Capital. Not in any meaningful way. He is a presence that has a weight to it, the kind of person you notice without trying. She notices. She files it away: powerful, probably Royal Guard, dangerous to operate near, probably not dangerous to avoid. She moves on. She does not know they share blood. He does not know she exists. The irony sits in the background of both their lives, waiting for Year 10.

**Canon outcome if untouched:** Elsa hires Felt at approximately fifteen to steal Emilia's insignia. The job goes wrong. Reinhard saves Felt. The Insignia lights up in her hand. She is forced into the Selection against every instinct she has, and she channels all of it — the rage at being abandoned, the anger at institutions that made her life what it was, the ferocious love of Old Man Rom she has never said aloud — into a candidacy that is nothing like what any of the noble houses expected.

---

### CRUSCH KARSTEN, FELIX ARGYLE, AND PRINCE FOURIER

**Year 5 ages: ~16. Year 9 ages: ~20-21. Locations: Karsten Estate / Royal Capital.**

This is the module where the trio reaches its full form — and where it breaks.

**Years 5 through 7 — The Deepening:**

The three of them are approximately sixteen to eighteen across the early years of this module. They are not children anymore, and they have not yet been tested in the way that adults in their world are eventually tested. The friendship has had years to settle into the kind of durable trust that does not require maintenance — it simply exists, an assumption of the texture of each other's lives.

Felix has built his armor completely by this point. The playfulness, the sharpness, the deliberate performance of ease — it is not dishonest, exactly. It is the form he chose for himself out of the available forms, a self assembled in the aftermath of nearly a decade of darkness with Crusch and Fourier as the primary architects. He is the best healer in the Kingdom. He knows this. He has done things with water magic that trained physicians in the capital consider impossible and then quietly ask him to do again. The dungeon is behind him. He does not talk about it. It is not behind him.

Crusch at sixteen to eighteen is becoming the person who will run one of the most formidable campaigns in the Royal Selection. She trains in swordsmanship and wins. She studies the Kingdom's political landscape and forms opinions — clear, direct, occasionally startling — that she does not soften for her audience. She has her father Meckart's approval and her mother Helena's absence and Fourier's warmth and Felix's loyalty, and she is building something out of these things that she does not yet have a name for.

Fourier at sixteen to eighteen is a genuinely good prince in a country that does not often produce them. He is enthusiastic, deeply sincere, the kind of person who makes a room feel warmer by entering it. He is growing into something that might one day be a genuinely good monarch — not because he is brilliant or strategic or ruthless, but because he actually listens to people and means it when he tells them he will try. He is in love with Crusch in the specific way of someone who has been in love for so long he has forgotten it is called that. He thinks of it as simply the way things are — Crusch is just what the world looks like when it is working.

**Year 8 — The Plague and Felix's Campaign:**

Felix is summoned to the Royal Castle when the pattern of the illness becomes undeniable. He goes. He does not leave for months. He works with the specific, grinding intensity of a person who knows they are the best available option and that the best available option may not be enough.

He identifies what the illness is doing — tracking its progress through water magic, learning the signature of it in the body's mana flow. He understands, gradually, that the mechanism is not organic. The plague is not spreading from person to person. It is selecting. It is finding the royal bloodline by some means he cannot see, cannot interrupt, cannot redirect. He can buy time — hours and days with careful work — but he cannot cure it.

He does not tell Fourier this. He tells Fourier he is working on it. He stays at the bedside. He does not stop working.

Crusch is there when she is allowed to be, and she holds the shape of herself with tremendous effort. Felix watches her hold it. He does not tell her to stop. He does not tell her it is allowed to fall apart. He does not have the words for this — he has only the presence, which he gives without condition or limit.

**Year 9 — Fourier's Death:**

Fourier dies at approximately twenty. The exact moment is not dramatized in canon in detail — what is given is its aftermath: Felix at a deathbed, unable to perform the miracle he promised himself he would perform; Crusch afterward, converting something enormous into something harder and colder and precise.

Fourier died well. This is not comfort — it is the true thing. He was not afraid, not at the end. He made Felix laugh one more time. He told Crusch she was going to be extraordinary. He believed both things. He died believing them.

Felix carries this for the rest of his life in the specific way a healer carries the person they could not save. He does not speak about it easily. He does not stop being Felix — the armor holds, because he built it for exactly this kind of weight. But Fourier is the shape of the thing underneath the armor, and will always be.

Crusch converts. This is the only word for what she does with the grief: she takes it in and it comes out as iron. The White Whale campaign that will define her candidacy in Arc 1 is built on this — not the calculation, not the strategy, not the political positioning. The foundation is Fourier's death and the refusal to let the world take anything else she loves without a fight.

**The Selection:**

When the Selection is called, Crusch enters it. Not because she wanted the throne before Year 9 — that ambition was not yet fully formed. She enters it because the Selection is the shape the world has taken, and she will not step aside from the world's shape when there is work to be done inside it. Felix is her knight. He stands where Fourier would have stood, one person doing the work of two people, which is the only math he has available.

**If Fourier is alive:**

If the plague was prevented — if the user found the source, identified the mechanism, intervened in time — then Fourier is alive at Module 4's close. He is approximately nineteen or twenty, growing into a good prince in a kingdom that has its heir. The Selection is never called. The trio does not break.

What the trio becomes without the loss depends entirely on how the years of this module played out. But the central truth is this: Crusch does not become the iron commander. She becomes something else — perhaps something better, perhaps something less forged, perhaps something that required the forge and will have to find its tempering elsewhere. Felix does not carry the healer's failure. Fourier lives. These three people, who were going to be defined by grief, are instead defined by what they build together when the catastrophe does not arrive.

The noble houses, without a Selection to maneuver within, do not simply stop scheming. They find other targets. The pressure the Selection would have channeled into managed competition disperses into the Kingdom's existing structure, finding every weakness. The world has not become safer because Fourier lived. It has become different. Different, in this story, means the story has to find new shapes for what was going to happen — and so does everyone in it.

**Canon outcome if untouched:** Fourier dies. The trio breaks in the specific way that makes them who they are in Arc 1. Felix and Crusch carry the grief into the work and the work into the fight. They are extraordinary. They are heartbroken. The Selection unfolds. The White Whale is still out there.

### RAM & REM

**Year 5 ages: ~12. Year 9 ages: ~16-17. Location: Roswaal Mansion.**

The twins have been at the Roswaal Mansion for approximately five years at the start of this module. The acute grief of Year 0 — the village, the horn, the fire — has settled into the architecture of who they are. They are no longer processing it. They have built themselves on top of it.

**Ram at twelve to sixteen-seventeen:**

Ram's horn is gone. The power that should have made her extraordinary — the wind magic that should have grown to levels no living Oni could match — is a fraction of what it should be. She can still use it. She is still formidable by any standard that does not compare her to what she was. But she knows what she lost. She touches the scar sometimes, in private, and knows.

What she has built in the absence of the power: a precision of observation that approaches something supernatural. Ram cannot overpower a room. She can read it — every current, every unspoken thing, every gap between what someone says and what they mean. She has learned to be the sharpest person in any room she enters, not because she has the most force available but because she uses what she has better than anyone else uses what they have.

Her devotion to Roswaal has deepened into something she does not examine. He saved her. He gave her a home. He is the only solid thing in a world that burned everything else down. She loves him in the way a person loves the only thing they have left after a catastrophe — completely, without armor, without the examination that might reveal the thing she is loving is not what it appears to be. She does not know he let the village burn. If she knew, the world she rebuilt would shatter again. She does not know.

Her relationship with Rem is complicated in the way that Ram and Rem's relationship is always complicated — profound love tangled up with a guilt structure that neither of them designed and neither of them can resolve without the other one's cooperation, which neither of them wants to ask for. Ram does not want Rem to feel guilty. Rem cannot stop. This is a conversation they have never had and both have every day in different ways.

**Rem at twelve to sixteen-seventeen:**

Rem has transformed the guilt into work. This is her solution, and it is a complete one in the sense that it functions — she is an exceptional servant, an extraordinary cook, a careful housekeeper, a person who anticipates needs before they are articulated and fulfills them with a precision that borders on devotion. The Roswaal Mansion runs more smoothly because of her than it does because of anyone else.

The inferiority complex does not resolve. It is never confronted directly, because confronting it would require Rem to say aloud the thing she believes: that she is less than Ram, that the horn's loss was a trade the universe made at the wrong exchange rate, that her life has been given value she did not earn by an accident of survival. She does not say this. She works instead. The work is the argument against the belief — I am here, I am doing this, I am useful — but arguments against a belief do not dissolve it. They just occupy the space where the belief lives.

She is developing a ferocity. Not the aggressive, forward-facing ferocity of Ram — something different. A willingness to be entirely expended in service of something she has decided matters. Witch Cult hatred is the sharpest edge of it: everything that happened to them, to Ram, to the village, is located in the Cult. The hatred is clean and total and gives the guilt somewhere to go.

By Year 9, the twins are approximately sixteen to seventeen. Frederica has been their senior throughout. The household has become their home in the specific way that something becomes home when there is nowhere else to return to.

**Canon outcome if untouched:** The twins serve Roswaal through Emilia's arrival (Year 9) and into Arc 1. They are seventeen at Arc 1's start. Ram is the sharp one. Rem is the devastating one. Both of them are defined by a night they were seven years old and the world they knew burned.

### EMILIA

**Year 5 apparent age: ~17-18. Year 9 apparent age: ~17-18. Location: Elior Forest.**
**Note: Emilia is a half-elf and does not visibly age. Her appearance remains ~17-18 throughout the entire post-waking period regardless of time passed.**

Emilia has been awake for two years at the start of this module. She has been awake for six years at its close. These years are quiet and hard in the specific way that quiet can be hard when the silence is full of faces you cannot reach.

Her routine is established: the glinstone trade, the frozen rounds, the morning ritual of wiping frost from the faces in the trees. She has learned the names of her frozen people — she knew them once, before the freeze, and she has pieced them back together from her slowly recovering memories, and she uses the names. She tells them what the seasons are doing. She does not know if they can hear her. She talks to them anyway. This is not madness. It is the refusal to treat them as objects simply because they cannot respond.

The village on the forest's outskirts has not warmed to her. A few individuals have. The man she trades with most reliably does not flinch when she comes to the stall anymore — he maintains a careful, respectful distance, but he does not hide. She counts this as progress. It has taken two years to achieve.

Puck is constant. He wakes with her. He teaches her — the properties of different spirits, the theory of contract-binding, the history of the world she missed while she was asleep, delivered in pieces small enough not to overwhelm. He does not tell her everything he knows. He tells her what she can carry. The contract between them is the most stable thing in her life, and the stability is not the comfort of safety — it is the comfort of being witnessed by someone who chose to stay.

**The Accumulation of Solitude:**

Six years of this shapes a person in specific ways. Emilia is resilient in a way that is not cheerful — it is the resilience of someone who has survived long stretches of being completely on their own and discovered they can keep going past the point where they expected to stop. She is self-sacrificing to a degree that occasionally alarms Puck: she will deny herself comfort, company, warmth, to serve the frozen people who cannot ask her to. She has decided this is what she is for.

She has not decided she deserves more than this. The world's response to her face — the running, the shuttering, the flinching — has been consistent enough to calcify into a background assumption: she is tolerated, at best, and her role is to make that toleration as easy as possible by not asking for anything. She is useful. Being useful is the form of acceptable existence available to her.

She is not broken by this understanding. She functions inside it with a grace that is its own kind of strength. But it is a cage she has built out of other people's fear, and she has not yet found the person who refuses to let her stay inside it.

**Puck's Worry:**

Puck watches her and worries in the specific way an old spirit worries about a young person he loves who is becoming too good at surviving without joy. He does not press. He shows up. He calls her Lia. He makes sure she laughs at least once a day, because a day without laughter is a day that is grinding her down without her noticing. He tells her she is remarkable — not in the way of praise, in the way of fact, because he is very old and has met very few people and she is the most remarkable person he has ever met and he does not want her to not know that.

He knows Roswaal is coming. He knows the shape of what is coming because he is old enough to see the arc of things, and the arc of things bends toward the forest at Year 9. He has decided he will not prevent it. What Emilia needs — the frozen people, the world beyond the trees — requires the kind of power that neither of them can access alone. Roswaal will come with a path. Emilia will take it. Puck will be there for all of it.

**Roswaal Arrives — Year 9:**

Roswaal L. Mathers arrives at Elior Forest in Year 9. He is not subtle about his approach — he is not the kind of person who benefits from subtlety, and Puck is not the kind of spirit who fails to notice a Great Magic User entering his territory. The resulting exchange of power is not brief. They fight, in the specific way two very old, very powerful beings fight when neither is committed to killing the other — a prolonged, careful test of what the other is made of.

It ends. Roswaal introduces himself. He explains the Selection. He presents the Dragon Insignia. It confirms what he already knew: Emilia is eligible.

He tells her what she needs to hear: there is a path to freeing her people, and it runs through the throne of the Dragon Kingdom.

He does not tell her what he wants from her. He does not tell her what his Gospel predicted. He does not tell her about Echidna. He gives her the truth in the exact proportions that will produce the answer he needs.

She looks at the frozen people in the trees. She takes the Insignia. She says yes.

**If someone reached Emilia before Roswaal:**

The Frozen Bonds events (Module 3) established the contact. The years between then and now have built whatever relationship was built. What Roswaal finds at the forest's edge in Year 9 is not a solitary girl desperate for any path forward. It is a girl who has people — at least one person, whatever the user built across these years — and who therefore evaluates his offer from a position of partial security rather than complete isolation.

This changes the negotiation. Emilia can ask questions. She can push back. She can weigh his offer against alternatives she did not know existed before someone showed her they existed. She may still accept Roswaal's patronage — the throne is still the path to freeing her people, and Roswaal is still offering it — but she accepts it as someone who has options, not as someone who has no choice. This is not what Roswaal's Gospel predicted. His book described a girl who would accept his offer without condition. What he finds is someone who has conditions.

**Canon outcome if untouched:** Emilia accepts Roswaal's offer. She is brought first to the Miload Manor, then to the Mathers Estate. She learns about the Kingdom, the Selection, what it means to exist in a world that knows her face as Satella's face. She has Puck. She has learned how to have exactly one person, and she is about to learn how difficult it is to let more than one person in. The frozen people remain in the ice. The Selection begins.

### OTTO SUWEN

**Year 5 age: ~16. Location: Picoutatte.**
**Exiled approximately Year 6, age ~17.**
**Year 9 age: ~21. Location: Wandering merchant, various locations in Lugunica.**

At sixteen, Otto is still in Picoutatte — still growing up in a merchant household, still managing his Divine Protection with increasing competence, still slightly strange in the specific way he has always been slightly strange. Frufoo is a constant companion. His older brother is the only family member who knows the truth.

**The Exile — Year 6:**

The incident happens at approximately seventeen. Through the ambient chatter of his Protection, he becomes aware of a noblewoman's private affair with a man who is not her husband. Otto, seventeen and still learning where the line sits between information-he-has and information-it-is-safe-to-share, mentions it. He does not think of it as gossip. He thinks of it as simply a thing that is true, in the same category as weather reports and road conditions, both of which his Protection also provides. The noblewoman does not see it this way.

She uses her influence to banish him from Picoutatte. She sends an assassin after him. The assassin finds him. The assassin fails — not because Otto fights them off but because the Protection's ambient awareness of the world around him gives him enough warning to run at the right moment, and because the assassin was hired at a rate that did not reflect the task's actual difficulty, and because Otto is, by this point, specifically good at navigating through a world that is not particularly on his side.

He leaves. He takes Frufoo. He says goodbye to his brother. He does not go back.

**Life as a Wandering Merchant — Years 6 to 9:**

Otto Suwen, wandering merchant, is talented at his trade in ways that are not visible on the surface. What is visible on the surface: a young man with an earnest face and a ground dragon and a string of business ventures that fail to be as profitable as they should be, given the hours he puts in and the intelligence he clearly possesses. What is not visible on the surface: the specific, inexplicable way that the world's minor catastrophes locate Otto Suwen and set up camp nearby.

He is not stupid. He is not unskilled. He is the victim of a probability field that seems personally interested in finding new ways to set him back without quite finishing him. His first hauling contract fails because the road floods. His second fails because the goods are the wrong type for the regional tariff that was updated the week before he arrived. His third almost doesn't fail, and then fails in a way that is deeply unfair and specifically funny if you are not the one who loses the money.

He keeps going. This is the thing about Otto that the failures obscure: he keeps going. Every setback is processed, catalogued, and converted into a reason to try a different angle. He is not optimistic — he has no illusions about his luck. He is persistent in the way of someone who has run the numbers and concluded that stopping is worse than continuing, regardless of the intermediate results.

By Year 9, Otto is approximately twenty-one. He has been on the road for three years. He is not successful in any conventional sense. He is, however, alive and slightly better at his trade than he was when he started, which given the probability field operating against him represents an extraordinary achievement.

He does not know he will meet Subaru. He does not know that the most important thing he will ever do in his life is show up for someone who does not expect to be shown up for. He is currently worrying about his next invoice.

**Canon outcome if untouched:** Otto's wandering road eventually brings him to the events of Arc 1. He and Subaru first interact when Otto inadvertently gets caught up in the Emilia Camp's movements near the Mathers Estate. He hates Subaru briefly, with complete justification. He helps him anyway. He keeps helping him. He becomes one of the most loyal people in Subaru's life because he is the kind of person who, when presented with someone in genuine need, concludes that the correct response is to help — regardless of the personal cost.

Frederica has been Head Maid at the Roswaal Mansion for five years at the start of this module. She has trained Ram and Rem. She has maintained the household. She has written letters to Garfiel that he does not respond to, or responds to with anger. She has kept writing.

### GARFIEL TINZEL

**Year 5 age: ~9. Year 9 age: ~13-14. Location: The Sanctuary.**

Garfiel is nine at the start of this module. He has been the Sanctuary's self-appointed guardian for approximately five years — since the year his mother left and his sister followed and he decided that the only way to keep what remained was to make certain nothing else could leave.

He is ferocious in a way that his age does not fully explain. He trains constantly. His beast-human heritage has begun expressing more strongly as he grows — the transformation into partial or full tiger form is becoming available to him, a power he practices with the specific intensity of a child who has decided that power is the only reliable thing. **Lewes Meyer** — or the Ryuzu clone who serves as the Sanctuary's matriarch — watches him with patience and something that operates like love. He has accepted her as the stable presence his family stopped being. She is the Sanctuary. The Sanctuary does not leave.

By Year 9, Garfiel is approximately thirteen to fourteen. He is remarkable for his age — a fighter who would be formidable in any context, made more so by a furious commitment to the training that gives his days shape. He is also, still, a child — and the things that are most child-like about him are the things he has least language for: the earnestness, the loyalty, the way his face changes when someone he trusts treats him with genuine warmth. He has not had a lot of warmth to practice receiving.

He has not forgiven Frederica. He knows, abstractly, that she writes. He does not write back, or writes back badly — short, angry things that do not say what he means because he does not know what he means. He means: *I was four years old and you left and the world ended and I built something out of the wreckage and I am terrified to look at you because what if looking at you confirms that I built the wrong thing.* He does not have those words. He has one-line responses and then silence.

**If someone reached the Sanctuary during the prequel years:** Garfiel's development depends entirely on what was built. A Garfiel who has had even one person demonstrate that the outside world contains something worth reaching toward is different from the canonical one, who constructed his entire identity around the premise that the outside world only takes. Even partial contact — someone who came through the Sanctuary's barrier, spent time there, left without betrayal — can crack the architecture of that belief before it fully calcifies.

**Canon outcome if untouched:** Garfiel reaches approximately thirteen to fourteen at Module 4's close. He continues growing into the self-appointed guardian — more powerful, more entrenched, more committed to the logic that keeping people inside keeps them safe. Arc 4 arrives and challenges everything he has built. He resists. He breaks. He becomes someone who has left the barrier and discovered the outside world did not kill him. He is the best version of himself, finally, on the other side of the grief he never processed.
